quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to move your final presentation to a later date because of a clash with a medical procedure. Arrange the body of the email to your module tutor. Subject: Request to present on 27 May instead / Greeting: Dear Dr Hale,
options: I have a hospital procedure booked for 19 and 20 May, and my doctor has advised that I should rest afterwards.
I can send a letter from the hospital, and I have already prepared my slides, so I would be ready on the new date.
I am writing to ask whether I could give my final presentation on 27 May instead of 20 May.

Thank you for considering this.

Yours sincerely,
Bronwen Solomon
quests.hint: Request, reason, evidence, thanks.
quests.explanation: Two purposes are combined here, a request and an explanation. The request comes first so the tutor knows what is being asked, then the reason makes it credible. The offer of evidence and mention of readiness reduces the tutor's effort.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A tenant asks the landlord for permission to keep a small dog and explains why. Piece together the email.
options:
I work from home and would be present most of the day, and I am happy to pay an additional deposit or provide a reference from my vet.

I would be grateful for your decision by the end of the month.

Kind regards,
Olusola Bakare
Dear Mrs Coleman,
I would like to ask whether I may adopt a small rescue dog, a five-kilo terrier, and keep it in my flat.
Subject: Request for permission to keep a small dog, flat 9
quests.hint: State the request, then reassure the landlord's likely concerns, then give a time frame.
quests.explanation: The explanation in this email answers the landlord's worries (noise, damage) rather than only telling your story. Ending with a time frame gives a clear next step.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A team member asks to attend a training course and explains the benefit to the business. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Request to attend the Data Visualisation course / Dear Mr Peters, / Kind regards, Aisling Byrne). Arrange the body.
options: I would like to request approval to attend the two-day Data Visualisation course in Leeds on 3 and 4 July.
I would be happy to discuss this at our one-to-one.
The course costs £420, and the travel costs would be about £60.
The skills would help me produce clearer dashboards for the sales team, which we have discussed as a priority.
quests.hint: The manager decides using the benefit, so join it to the request, then give the cost.
quests.explanation: The request comes first. Linking the course to a stated team priority makes it a business case. Cost comes after benefit so the manager reads the price in context.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are enquiring about a wedding venue and stating when you are free to visit. Structure the email.
options: We are planning a wedding for around 80 guests on Saturday 6 September, and we are interested in hiring the Orchard Barn.

Could you tell me if the date is still available and what your packages cost?

We could visit on any weekday afternoon or on Sunday 22 June.

Yours faithfully,
Priyanka and Ryan Fernandes
Subject: Enquiry about a wedding on 6 September
Dear Events Manager,
quests.hint: First the event, then the questions, then your availability to visit.
quests.explanation: The venue must know the date and number of guests to answer. Once they respond, your availability tells them when to offer a viewing, so it works best at the end.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You would like private tutoring and need to say when you are free. Arrange the email.
options: Dear Mr Adamu,
Subject: Enquiry about maths tutoring for a Year 10 student
I am looking for a tutor for my son, who is in Year 10 and has a GCSE exam in June. Do you have any availability, and what is your hourly rate?

We would prefer weekday evenings after 5 pm, but we can be flexible.

Kind regards,
Deirdre Malone
quests.hint: Introduce the need, ask, and then give the times that work.
quests.explanation: The tutor first needs to know what help is required and if he has space. Your preferred times follow because they matter only when he has a place to offer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are contacting a photographer and asking about services and dates. Put together the email.
options: I saw your portrait work at the community fair and would like to book a family session for six people in October.
Hello Ms Oyelaran,

Could you send me your prices and let me know which weekends you have free?

Best wishes,
Karl Petersen
Subject: Family portraits in October: availability and prices
quests.hint: Explain why you are contacting this person, then ask for both pieces of information.
quests.explanation: Naming where you saw her work explains why you chose her. Asking about prices and availability in one sentence lets her answer both in a single reply.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A company sent the wrong product to a customer. Assemble the apology and solution.
options: I am sorry that we sent you a blue kettle instead of the white one you ordered.
Dear Ms Yildiz,
Subject: Apology and replacement for order 88214

A white kettle will be sent today by next-day delivery, and you can keep the blue one at no charge.

We apologise again for the inconvenience.

Yours sincerely,
Liam Ogunbanjo, Customer Care
quests.hint: Apology first, then the remedy. The final line reinforces the apology.
quests.explanation: In a two-purpose email, the apology and the solution must both be visible. The remedy is specific (which day, what happens to the wrong item), which makes the apology believable.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You missed a deadline at work and want to apologise and propose a new plan. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Apology for the late report and a new timetable / Dear Ms Dixon, / Kind regards, Edwin Tay). Arrange the body.
options: I am sorry that I did not deliver the report on Friday as agreed.
I will send you a complete draft by noon on Wednesday, and I will send a progress update tomorrow afternoon.
Thank you for your understanding.
I underestimated how long the data cleaning would take.
quests.hint: Take responsibility, give the new date, and add a checkpoint.
quests.explanation: The apology names the cause honestly without making excuses. A new date and an interim update reassure your manager that the problem is under control.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You cancelled a friend's visit at the last minute. Apologise and suggest a new plan. Arrange the email.
options: I'm so sorry for cancelling on Saturday at the last minute, especially since you'd already cooked.
Subject: Sorry about Saturday
Hi Freya,

How about I come round next Sunday instead and bring dessert this time?

Let me know if that suits you.

Love,
Theodora
quests.hint: Apologise for the specific act, then offer a way to make it up.
quests.explanation: 'Especially since you'd already cooked' shows you understand the impact. Proposing a new visit with dessert turns the apology into a concrete plan.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are confirming a job interview and need to ask about parking. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Confirming interview on Monday 16 June at 10:30 / Dear Ms Ikeda, / Kind regards, Amos Turner). Arrange the body.
options: Could you tell me whether there is parking near the office or a place nearby that you would recommend?
I will be coming by car.
Thank you for the invitation.
I am writing to confirm that I will attend the interview on Monday 16 June at 10:30.
quests.hint: Confirm first so the reader's main need is met, then add the question.
quests.explanation: The confirmation is the urgent business matter, so it comes first. A follow-up question is easier to answer when the main point is settled.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A supplier confirms an order and asks for a missing detail. Structure the message.
options: Dear Mr Fontana,
Thank you for your order of 500 leaflets, which will be printed on 12 June.

Could you tell us whether you would like them delivered to your office or collected from our shop?

Kind regards,
PrintWorks Team
Subject: Order 9034 confirmed: one detail needed
quests.hint: The customer wants to know the order is confirmed before being asked for more.
quests.explanation: Confirming receipt first reassures the customer. The question follows because production can't be completed without the answer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are confirming a lunch with a friend and checking a food preference. Build the message.
options:
I've booked the Italian place near the station. Is that okay, or would you prefer somewhere vegetarian?

See you soon,
Jude
Hi Anita,
Subject: Lunch on Friday still on?
I just wanted to check that we're still on for lunch on Friday at 12:30.
quests.hint: Confirm the plan, then share the choice and invite a change.
quests.explanation: The check-in comes first. Presenting the restaurant as a decision that can be changed keeps the tone flexible.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are reporting a faulty machine at work and asking for a repair. Arrange the email.
options:
Could you arrange an engineer to visit today if possible? We have a large mailing to prepare for tomorrow.

Thank you,
Cleo Rodrigues
Dear Facilities Team,
The photocopier on floor 3 has displayed an error message since this morning and will not print or copy.
Subject: Photocopier on floor 3 out of order: please arrange repair
quests.hint: State the problem, then the requested action, then the reason for urgency.
quests.explanation: The subject holds both the problem and the action. The body gives evidence, and the closing explains the urgency, which helps the team prioritise.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A resident is reporting a broken streetlight and requesting repair. Assemble the email.
options: Dear Highways Department,
The streetlight outside 27 Coronation Road has been out since 3 October, and the street is very dark after 5 pm.
Subject: Broken streetlight outside 27 Coronation Road

I would be grateful if you could arrange a repair, as several older residents use this street.

Yours faithfully,
Mr S. Farouk
quests.hint: Location, problem and safety reason should be combined with a request.
quests.explanation: Giving the location and the length of time helps the council act. Mentioning older residents explains why it matters without exaggeration.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are pointing out a mistake in a shared spreadsheet and asking a colleague to correct it. Lay out the email.
options: Hi Corinne,

Could you correct it before the report goes to Finance tomorrow?

Thanks,
Joseph
I think the March total in the travel sheet is £1,240 rather than £1,420, as two digits appear to have been swapped.
Subject: Small error in the March figures
quests.hint: Point out the error kindly and state what should happen next.
quests.explanation: Using 'appear to have been swapped' avoids blame, and stating the correct number saves the colleague time. The deadline explains why it should be corrected now.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together the email inviting colleagues to a leaving party and asking for a reply.
options: Subject: Leaving drinks for Beatriz: Friday 4 July, please RSVP

Please let me know by Monday 30 June if you can come, so I can book enough tables.

Best wishes,
Holly
Dear all,
Beatriz is leaving after eleven years, and we would love you to join us for drinks at The Anchor on Friday 4 July from 6 pm.
quests.hint: The invitation gives the occasion, time and place; the RSVP gives the deadline and the reason.
quests.explanation: A good invitation makes the event attractive and the response easy. Explaining why you need a reply by Monday (booking tables) encourages people to answer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email inviting a client to an open day and asking for confirmation of numbers.
options:
Please tell us how many people will attend by Friday 2 May, and let us know about any dietary requirements.

Kind regards,
Elena Marchetti
Subject: Invitation to our Open Day on 14 May
Dear Mr Rezaei,
We would be delighted if you and your colleagues could attend our Open Day on Wednesday 14 May from 10 am to 3 pm at our new offices.
quests.hint: Invitation, then two RSVP details, both with deadline.
quests.explanation: The invitation is warm and specific. Asking for numbers and dietary needs at once avoids a second email to collect them.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Structure the email inviting friends to a housewarming and asking whether they can bring a dish.
options: We've finally moved in, and we'd love you to come and see the flat on Saturday 12th from 4 pm.

If you can make it, please reply by Wednesday. Bringing a dish to share would be brilliant, but there's no pressure.

Lots of love,
Bea and Sunil
Hi everyone,
Subject: Housewarming on Saturday 12th!
quests.hint: The invitation is warm; the request is light.
quests.explanation: Optional requests ('no pressure') keep the tone friendly. The RSVP deadline is included so the hosts can plan food.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are updating a client that work is on track except for one part which will be late. Build the email.
options: The data collection is complete, and the analysis is progressing as planned.
Subject: Project update: revised date for the final report

However, the final report will now be ready on 27 June rather than 20 June, because we are waiting for one dataset from the regional office.

I will confirm the date again on Friday.

Kind regards,
Marcelo Dias
Dear Ms Krüger,
quests.hint: Good news first, then the change, then a plan.
quests.explanation: Two purposes here: update and revised deadline. Beginning with what is on track puts the delay in perspective. The commitment to confirm the date on Friday reduces uncertainty.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A student informs a supervisor of progress and asks to change a milestone. Put together the email.
options: Subject: Dissertation progress and revised submission of the literature review
Dear Dr Lee,

I would like to move the literature review deadline from 14 July to 21 July, as I found several important recent articles late.

Does this seem realistic to you?

Yours sincerely,
Dalia Njoroge
I have completed the first draft of the methodology chapter and attached it for your comments.
quests.hint: Progress before the request for change.
quests.explanation: A supervisor is more receptive to a change if progress has been shown. The closing question invites a conversation rather than demanding approval.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A team leader tells the team about progress and a revised deadline for a customer demo. Arrange the email.
options:
The client has asked to see the demo on Tuesday 8 July instead of Friday 4 July, which gives us an extra weekend for testing.

Let's use it to fix the reporting bugs.

Thanks,
Amara
Good progress this week: the login and search features are complete.
Subject: Demo moved to Tuesday 8 July
Hi team,
quests.hint: News that helps the team can be used to frame the new date positively.
quests.explanation: The team hears their success first. The new date is framed as extra time, and the closing gives a direction for the extra days.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to thank a former colleague and ask her for another favour. Lay out the email.
options:
I wonder whether you would mind looking at my CV before I send it to the second company. Even ten minutes of your time would help.

Many thanks,
Alejandro
Subject: Thank you, and a small favour
Thank you again for the introduction to Mr Kelly, which led to an interview last week.
Dear Sunita,
quests.hint: Say thank you for what happened, then ask for something new.
quests.explanation: Gratitude before a request makes the reader feel valued. The request should be small and specific to avoid feeling like an imposition.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A student thanks a librarian for previous help and requests access to a special collection. Piece together the email.
options: Subject: Access to the Whitfield archive

I have now learned that the Whitfield archive may contain related letters. Would it be possible to consult it on Thursday afternoon?

Yours sincerely,
Gwenllian Rees
Thank you for your help last week in finding the 1920s shipping records, which were very useful for my project.
Dear Ms Bogdanov,
quests.hint: Thanks, connection to the new need, request.
quests.explanation: Linking the new request to what she helped with shows continuity. Asking whether it is possible leaves her free to say no.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Thank you for your feedback / Dear Mr Adeleke, / Kind regards, Penelope Holt). Arrange the body.
options: I was delighted to hear that the team found it useful.
Thank you for your kind words about the training session.
I would be happy to send you the wording for approval.
Would you be willing to let us quote your comments on our website?
quests.hint: The request follows naturally from the thanks and gives the client control.
quests.explanation: Offering approval of the wording protects the client's interests, making a yes more likely.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A speaker must decline a talk in October but could offer another date. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Invitation to speak on 10 October / Dear Ms Sorensen, / Yours sincerely, Professor Ibrahim Waziri). Arrange the body.
options: Unfortunately I am not available on that date.
But I would be delighted to speak in the spring if you plan another event.
Thank you very much for inviting me to speak at your conference on 10 October.
I wish you a very successful conference.
quests.hint: Thanks, decline, alternative, good wishes.
quests.explanation: When declining, the alternative keeps the relationship active. A closing wish shows goodwill.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A manager declines a request for a pay rise but offers a review date. Build the email.
options: Dear Tobias,
Subject: Re: Your request about salary
Thank you for raising this, and for the work you have done this year.

I am not able to approve a rise at the moment, as budgets are frozen until January. I would like to review your salary at that point, and I can also look at training opportunities in the meantime.

Kind regards,
Cynthia Marsh
quests.hint: Acknowledge, refuse honestly, then give something constructive.
quests.explanation: A plain refusal with a reason is fairer than a vague answer. Offering a review date and training makes the refusal feel less final.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You cannot lend a friend your car but can offer a lift instead. Put together the reply.
options: Hi Matteo,

I could drive you to the airport on Saturday morning, though, if that helps.

Just tell me what time.

Cheers,
Dani
Subject: Re: Borrowing the car
Sorry, but I can't lend the car this weekend, because my insurance only covers me.
quests.hint: Refuse clearly, explain simply, offer what you can.
quests.explanation: A short reason makes the refusal understandable. The alternative shows you still want to help.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Assemble the email that thanks a speaker, sends a photo and asks about a future date.
options: On behalf of the society, I would like to thank you for your talk on Tuesday, which many students described as inspiring.
Dear Dr Pereira,

I have attached three photos from the evening. Would you be willing to speak again next term?

Yours sincerely,
Eszter Dale
Subject: Thank you for speaking, and photos from the event
quests.hint: Thanks, then a small courtesy, then a future request.
quests.explanation: Thanks comes first because it is the emotional centre. The photos are a friendly extra, and the invitation is placed last.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email that apologises for a mix-up, confirms the corrected booking and asks for feedback.
options: Subject: Corrected booking and our apology

Your reservation is now correctly recorded for 21 to 24 July.

We would be grateful if you could tell us how your stay compares with your expectations when you check out.

Yours sincerely,
Daphne Reyes
Dear Mr Fitzgerald,
I am sorry that your booking showed the wrong dates in the confirmation we sent on Monday.
quests.hint: Apology, correction, then a low-pressure request.
quests.explanation: Three purposes appear in a natural order: correct the mistake, confirm the fact, then ask for something in return.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together the email that updates a team on progress, confirms the next meeting and requests input.
options:
Our next meeting is on Thursday 10 July at 10 am in Room 2. Please send me any topics you want to add to the agenda by Tuesday.

Thanks,
Olaf
Hi all,
We have finished the first phase and are a week ahead of schedule.
Subject: Progress, next meeting and a request
quests.hint: Good news, logistics, request.
quests.explanation: Because the email combines several purposes, it moves from the most general (progress) to the most specific (what you need). Each purpose has its own paragraph.
